definition: Multi-document summarization is an automatic procedure aimed at extraction of information from multiple texts written about the same topic.
details: The resulting summary report allows individual users, such as professional information consumers, to quickly familiarize themselves with information contained in a large cluster of documents. In such a way, multi-document summarization systems are complementing the news aggregators performing the next step down the road of coping with information overload.
story: Think of a lightbulb moment: the idea was always there, but someone had to point a finger at it. In plain words: Multi-document summarization is an automatic procedure aimed at extraction of information from multiple texts written about the same topic. Here is how it actually plays out: The resulting summary report allows individual users, such as professional information consumers, to quickly familiarize themselves with information contained in a large cluster of documents. Once you see it, you cannot unsee it. And that idea, made concrete, is Multi-document summarization.
